about: Every visible shape on the F/A-18C, region by region, with the reference photos that show it and whether the model matches (../verify/README.md, step 7). status: matches, wrong (with what is wrong), or unchecked. Numbers are the photo match's (photos.json) or the facts check's (check.py) as of the date; a shape inside the outline is only ever verified here.

nose.note: TM-101724's sections within 0.3 in; nose top outlines within 0.1-1 in in five photos
5.6 deg on its axis through the apex (was 6.7)
the seam cast onto the skin in dvids9820808 lies at FS 128.0 at the top and the bottom, against tm101724's 128.5; the gun slot ends ahead of it at FS 122.9. A paint line (nose.junction)

a shell on the skin from FS 144.9 to 187.4, its lower corners where the three photos' sight lines meet the skin (37 deg round from the top; was 26). No solved photo sees its upper edge: tm101724's, 15 deg round, which an overhead photo of another jet (dvids3435192, unsolved) agrees with
built from dvids9820808 (strut root FS 172.4-176.8, tip FS 163.7); tm101724 gives FS 164 to 177. Both tubes land on the photos' in dvids9820799 and dvids9820782

nose.shape: angle-of-attack probes, ECM and antenna fairings
nose.note: AOA probes at FS 164.0, WL 103.6, sized in dvids8678631; ECM covers from tm101724 (the photos agree within 1 in); the antenna fairings above the light strip and on the gun bay door from both sides' photos (how far they stand proud is estimated). The blade under the nose is built; the small comb antennas and fairing under the radome (FS 134-149) are not
the nose strips built flush in the lights material, FS 130.2-165.7 at WL 113.9, 1.7 in tall (both sides agree within 0.6 in). The wingtip and fin strips are light points only

canopy.shape: windscreen base, bow, crown and aft end
canopy.note: placed from the photos (windscreen 2 in higher, bow 2.3 in higher, aft end 4 in further aft than before); canopy outlines within 0.3-2 in from the side

the section is drawn in above the sill until it meets the photo-measured sill: the bow foot within 0.4 in, the traced sills within 0.5-0.8 in median (were 2.2-2.5); the body fades back out over 8 in below, with no ledge
both lean as the photos have them: the bow from its top at FS 235.8 to its foot at 239.9, the aft edge from 325 to the corner at 320.4 (the loft's rings move column by column)

the top line behind the crown read off two profiles (was 0.5-1.3 in high); the glass a superellipse from the sill, rounder at the bow and pointier aft, fitted to the outlines: their median miss 0.28 in (1.00 before)
headbox, helmet, HUD frame and glareshield edge where dvids9820808 shows them through the canopy; widths, tub, panel and limbs estimated. Not yet seen against a photo with the canopy open

lex.note: TM-101724's spans within 0.4 in; traced edges within 0.8-1.7 in in seven photos
moved 8 in aft and 5 in down to where seven photos put it

lex.shape: LEX upper surface across its span
lex.note: was a straight slope root to edge, 4.6 in low mid-span; now TP-3111's traced fall. The photographed fence tops caught it

was a square end standing 9.5 in above the wing root; now a fairing settling onto the nacelle shoulder and wing (shape.lex). It dived onto the nacelle growing in behind the inlet's plug and let the fuselage and inlet through in ragged patches (shape.seam: 72-110 sq in a side); it now settles toward the fuselage as it stands where the nacelle joins, clears the skin's corners and the wing's root, and nothing pokes through. Not yet seen in a photo from above
built: tp3111's base, the photos' top corners (within 1.6 in), 8.9 in tall over the LEX (tp3111: 8.3)

lex.shape: LEX slot and boarding ladder well
lex.note: the ladder stows inside the left LEX, its rails on the line with the most room between the LEX's skins (was 4.5 in below it); the well's outline and the slot not built

inlets.note: the D-shaped mouth from the photo match (layout.inlet): every lip point within 1.1 in, each traced lip edge within 0.6 in median; the duct's hydraulic diameter 23.6 in against tm103703's 23.34. The duct's plug renders grey where the real duct is dark: a paint matter

its leading edge upright at FS 381, bowing 2.7 in outboard at mid-height, within 0.2 in of all four traces; it stands 2-6 in off the fuselage. Its bleed perforations and the diverter fairing behind it are not built

falls from the lip's bottom (WL 76.8) onto the nacelle's line (73.6 at FS 447), where it rose 10 in into a nacelle section bottomed at WL 87; it eases from the mouth's D into the fuselage's own outline and hands over at FS 440 on one ring, where the two skins overlapped and crossed from FS 430 to 459 (shape.seam)

wing.note: cr201687's planform within 0.5 in; the underside photo's edges within 1-2 in on the right wing (4.3 in on the left's leading edge, its camera the weakest)
cr3608's 5% to 3.5% stations (was linear root to tip)

parked, as the user chose: the anhedral is the photos', -1.35 deg (cr201687 has -3), turning the wing about the LEX junction so the ground photo's tips fall within 0.5 in. The three in-flight photos put the tips another 5 in higher (4.6-5.4 leaving each out): the wing bent up at 1 g, a task of its own (wing flex). tips.py
folds 90-plus degrees to NATOPS's 27 ft 6 in (was 1 radian, 33 ft 3 in)
areas match cr201687; spans read off tp209033's sketch

not settled: the underside photo shows the leading edge stepping about 2.6 in (7 px) where the outer pylon hides it, and no source mentions a snag. Needs a sharper view of the leading edge at the fold

fins.note: moved 8 in aft and 7 in outboard to where nine photos put the tips; leading edges now within 0.1-0.5 in in most photos

stabilators.note: cr201687's within 0.6 in; moved 2.4 in aft for the 56 ft length

the root at WL 106.8 (was the sketches' 100), where three in-flight photos put the tips' leading corners (within 0.9 in leaving each out), at the engine axes' height; the HATP side view draws them about 10 in higher. The spindle is not published (provisional, through the mean chord's quarter point)

fuselage.note: outlines within 1-2 in from the rear, 4 in in dvids8678629; but the spine joints' seams triangulate 5-9 in inboard of the skin at WL 134-140 from FS 440 to 521 (three camera pairs): the spine is too broad there (a task)

each nacelle's bottom on the HATP side view's keel line (WL 73.3-74.1 over FS 436-472, rising to 78 by FS 540), within 0.4 in (layout.nacelle); dvids6696790's sky outline behind the left lip reads WL 73.6 at FS 447, the model 73.6. The earlier match to dvids9820808's belly line was the wrong edge: a tank and the open gear doors hang across the nacelle there. The navy photo's strip along the right nacelle falls at the same slope behind the lip and bottoms out near FS 490-500, but cannot fix its buttline

the speedbrake cut from the spine's own skin between the fins, 65 by 34 in (provisional; was 34 in to port, beside the left fin); the dorsal and spine blades built; 26 panel lines and the radome joint traced in five photos and cast onto the skin (layout.panels), most checked in a second photo within 0.1-1.3 in

tail.note: exit moved to FS 720 where four photos put its lower lip (tm101724's 54.4 ft is the HARV's)
a glowing liner deep in each nozzle for the engine to light, as wide as the throat at full reheat (tm101741's 348 in2); its depth is estimated

twelve outer flaps a nozzle, counted on three jets (12 brackets each side of one, a second's 12 trailing-edge gaps, a third's tabs 30 deg apart); flat facets with the exit's lowest lip where four photos put it. Their closing travel is tm101741's throat areas (provisional); the aft ends' stepped tabs are not built
stowed point moved to FS 684 (was 714); one photo

gear.note: track 124.7 in (was 116), nose wheels 13.3 in apart (was 10.4); axle heights set for NATOPS's static heights (the taxiing photos sit 1.4 deg nose down, the model 0.9)

provisional. Stowed inside the skin (shape.stowed): the main legs aft into the nacelles (NATOPS 2.10.1), 19 deg inboard with the wheels near flat, the two sides now mirrored; the nose bay's doors cut from the belly's skin, hinged at the bay's edges
